title: Replication package for "Battery charging, demand statistics and the evaluation of U.S. day-ahead load forecasts" (Zenodo, v1.2)
note: Dataset record by Liang-Cheng Chang (Shih Chien University), CC-BY-4.0. Code, derived data, results and four pre-specification documents for a manuscript said to be submitted to Energy Policy. Audits deteriorating day-ahead load forecasts in EIA-930 data for 49 US balancing authorities, 2018-2026, tracing each case against operator series, retail sales and documentation.

title: Zenodo record 24049915: scope and contents
note: Also quantifies how battery charging inside CAISO's published load changes forecast evaluation and reported demand growth, checks how other storage-reporting authorities treat charging, estimates weather-adjusted fleet forecast performance and re-scores benchmark comparisons. Ships 18 EIA-930 BALANCE files with a SHA-256 manifest; CAISO and SPP source files are not redistributed.

title: Zenodo record 24049915: caiso_accuracy_fullhours.json (preview)
note: CAISO day-ahead absolute percentage error, Jan-Oct, all hours. Against published load the yearly median rises from 1.568 (2021) to 3.566 (2026), the mean from 2.000 to 9.083. Net of charging: median 1.498 to 1.975, mean 1.873 to 2.551. Share of the rise removed by netting out charging: 0.761 (median), 0.904 (mean). Net 2026/2021 ratio: 1.32 (median), 1.36 (mean).

title: CHANGELOG_v1.2.md (Zenodo record 24049915)
note: v1.2 keeps the v1.0 archive and replaces one script and its output: shares are now computed from unrounded yearly values. Median share moves from 0.765 to 0.761, net median ratio from 1.31 to 1.32, mean share stays 0.904. Says the manuscript reports 76% (MdAPE), 90% (MAPE), a ratio of 1.32 and a rise of 0.48 points.

title: caiso_accuracy_fullhours.py (Zenodo record 24049915)
note: Short pandas script. Reads a merged CAISO table (forecast, published load, charging), keeps January-October hours, computes hourly absolute percentage error against published load and against load minus charging, takes yearly median and mean, then the share of the 2021-to-2026 rise that disappears on the net series. No model is fitted; the forecast is the operator's own.

title: EP_EIA930_replication_v1.0.zip file listing (Zenodo preview)
note: Listing only; file contents are not readable through the preview. Has LICENSE, README.md, requirements.txt, about 38 scripts, input archives (EIA-930, EIA-861, Open-Meteo, EIA reference tables), SHA-256 manifests, about 80 result files including benchmark re-scoring and weather-adjusted fleet results, and four prespecification files whose names carry the date 2026-11-01.

title: you-search: exact title of the manuscript
note: Query: the manuscript title in quotes, LinkedIn excluded, 20 results. No manuscript, preprint or journal page found. The only hit naming the package is a third-party GitHub issue listing new Zenodo battery datasets; the rest are unrelated EV-charging forecasting papers. No replication or critique of this package found.

title: jinnn11/grid-forecast-audit: day-ahead demand forecasts in EIA-930, 2016-2025 (README)
note: Separate public audit, first commit 28 Oct 2026, last 1 Nov 2026 (named by you-research). Finds three EIA-930 problems: CISO demand an hour late in two spans, CISO demand counting battery charging that its forecast omits, and the SWPP forecast diverging from SPP's own from 7 May 2025. With all three corrected, the 50-BA national error trend goes from 0.061 to 0.009 points a year.

title: jinnn11/grid-forecast-audit: limitations
note: States its own limits: the corrections were added after the pre-registered results were computed; only authorities whose forecasts looked bad were checked against operator data, so corrections tilt errors down; the cause of the SWPP change is unknown. No licence was visible in the fetched page. Its relation to the Zenodo package's author is not stated on either page.

title: grid-forecast-audit/results/ciso_check.md
note: CAISO check with OASIS data. In 2025 CAISO's day-ahead forecast is 6.9% below actual load; the hourly gap tracks charging (slope 0.90, R2 0.91) and not discharging. Against load less charging, bias goes to -0.6% and MAPE from 7.31% to 2.45%. About 377 MW an hour stays unexplained. Before 2021, with little storage, sampled months show bias within about 1.1%.

title: Form EIA-930 data format and transmittal instructions (EIA)
note: EIA's reporting rules. Electricity used to charge storage should be left out of actual demand and booked as negative net generation; a respondent that cannot do so may leave it in demand and report it separately under code DS. The day-ahead forecast is whatever the respondent produces in normal business and need not be consistent with demand as defined for the form.

title: 2024 Special Report on Battery Storage (CAISO, 29 May 2025)
note: From the you-research sources list; not fetched separately. CAISO's market monitor reports that battery charging was about 14.7% of load in the CAISO area in hours ending 10 to 13 during 2024, and that storage is modelled as a resource that can act as generation or load. Supports the size of charging, not the package's attribution figure.

title: cardinalgrid/ba-forecast-scorecard (README)
note: From the you-research sources list; not fetched separately. Another public scoring of balancing authorities' own day-ahead forecasts from EIA-930 (2015 to Sept 2026): demand-weighted MAPE 3.56% over 42 eligible authorities. Warns that high values often mean a data problem. Not a replication of the Zenodo package and does not address CAISO charging.

title: you-research (standard): which primary sources support or contradict the claim
note: One task, LinkedIn excluded, 7 sources. Answer says the package supports the three-quarters figure, EIA and CAISO documents support the mechanism, and one separate audit agrees on CAISO charging. It found no manuscript or preprint.
